lines.speaker: PETROV
lines.text: Lieutenant. Sit down. Take a tea before it gets cold.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: You wanted to speak with me, Sergeant?

lines.speaker: PETROV
lines.text: On the Eastern Front, in 1915, my unit found a thing near a village called Kholm. A thing the Germans were also looking for. Not a thing. A place.

lines.speaker: PETROV
lines.text: Twenty-three men with me. Three came back. None spoke of it after. Not even me.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: And why are you telling me this now?

lines.speaker: PETROV
lines.text: Because the last operation we ran… had the same smell. Listen to what the enemy says when they die, Lieutenant. Sometimes it is not German.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Petrov finishes the tea in silence and returns to the fire. He does not look at you again.

lines.speaker: PETROV
lines.text: You have a brother?

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Had. Henry. Loos, 1915.

lines.speaker: PETROV
lines.text: Ah. Loos. Body?

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: PETROV
lines.text: Mmh. Better sometimes. My brother I buried with these hands. I would have preferred not to.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You want to ask more, but he has already stood up.

lines.speaker: WREN
lines.text: Take off the coat. Let me see that arm.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: I'm fine, Doctor.

lines.speaker: WREN
lines.text: Everyone is fine. Until they are dead. Then they are quiet, which is different. Take off the coat.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: She examines the cut, cleans it with something that burns, stitches with uneven sutures.

lines.speaker: WREN
lines.text: I heard you shouting in the night. A woman's name?

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: My brother.

lines.speaker: WREN
lines.text: Ah. Worse still. Take this.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: What is it?

lines.speaker: WREN
lines.text: Basically whisky. Occupational habit.

lines.speaker: WREN
lines.text: Professional curiosity, Lieutenant. That last body you brought in. The one who died in Trench 47.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: What about him?

lines.speaker: WREN
lines.text: His heart had stopped three hours before I received him. And still he was warm.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Your mistake. Midday sun.

lines.speaker: WREN
lines.text: It rained all day, Lieutenant. There was no sun.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: She puts away her instruments with precise movements. She does not look at you.

lines.speaker: WREN
lines.text: Go sleep. Medical order.

lines.speaker: ASHCROFT
lines.text: Ah, Vale. Sit, sit. I was re-reading an interesting manuscript — a Coptic copy of a 4th-century text.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: In the middle of a war?

lines.speaker: ASHCROFT
lines.text: Especially in the middle of a war. Gnostic studies on what the ancients called the "Kenoma". The empty space between planes. Fascinating.

lines.speaker: ASHCROFT
lines.text: Some 2nd-century priests believed that certain places on earth were… thinner. That the barrier was more permeable there. Ancient wells. Crossroads. Battlefields.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: And you think that…

lines.speaker: ASHCROFT
lines.text: Ah, I think nothing. I am merely a collector of curiosities. But if you notice the smell of sea salt where there should be none, or light casting the wrong shadows — note the exact hour. Please. It is important for my research.

lines.speaker: ASHCROFT
lines.text: Have you ever thought about why this Salvage Corps exists, Lieutenant?

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: To contain incidents. That's what I was told.

lines.speaker: ASHCROFT
lines.text: Containment presupposes knowledge. Someone, in some dark office in Whitehall, knew enough to form this unit before you or I ever arrived here.

lines.speaker: ASHCROFT
lines.text: The question is: do they know because they studied? Or because they were warned?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He closes the manuscript slowly.

lines.speaker: ASHCROFT
lines.text: Anyway. Rest is important. Good night, Vale.

lines.speaker: WARDELL
lines.text: Lieutenant. Sit here, away from the fire. No one listens.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Do you have something to say, Corporal?

lines.speaker: WARDELL
lines.text: I've been at war since '14. Mons, Ypres, Somme. I haven't seen it all, but I've seen enough.

lines.speaker: WARDELL
lines.text: This unit is different. The officers don't ask where we've been. They only ask how many bodies we brought back. And sometimes they're annoyed when we bring some.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: What are you suggesting?

lines.speaker: WARDELL
lines.text: Suggesting? Nothing. Just warning you: when a mission starts to make sense, check twice. When it makes too much sense, check three times.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He lights a cigarette. His hand trembles almost imperceptibly.

lines.speaker: WARDELL
lines.text: You kill well, Lieutenant. I noticed.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Is that a compliment or an accusation?

lines.speaker: WARDELL
lines.text: Neither. An observation. You kill like someone finishing a task. No anger, no pleasure. Bosses like that.

lines.speaker: WARDELL
lines.text: Just be careful. A man who kills without feeling forgets that others feel. Then when the body falls, you don't understand why the rest of the unit goes quiet.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: And you? Do you feel?

lines.speaker: WARDELL
lines.text: I feel too much. That's why I'm still alive. Good night, Lieutenant.

lines.speaker: PETROV
lines.text: Lieutenant. You are pale.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Last night I heard a voice. Calling my name.

lines.speaker: PETROV
lines.text: A woman's voice?

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Yes. Did you hear it too?

lines.speaker: PETROV
lines.text: No. But in Kholm, this is how it began. Always a voice. Always calling a specific name. One person at a time.

lines.speaker: PETROV
lines.text: The three who survived with me — we all heard voices first. The twenty who died also heard. Hearing decides nothing.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: What decides?

lines.speaker: PETROV
lines.text: What you ANSWER. If you answer. And to whom.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Petrov takes a sip of tea. He does not look at you, but he does not leave either.

lines.speaker: WREN
lines.text: Lieutenant. Sit.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: I have no wounds today.

lines.speaker: WREN
lines.text: I did not ask. Sit.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You sit. She places a cold hand on your wrist, checks your pulse without looking at her watch.

lines.speaker: WREN
lines.text: Thirty-eight beats more than last week. You are falling asleep late. Eating little.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: War.

lines.speaker: WREN
lines.text: War is constant. You are not. I've seen three men fall apart this way before. Two died in the next combat. The third killed himself.

lines.speaker: WREN
lines.text: You will do neither. You will come back here tomorrow night. I'll give you something to sleep.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: I can't be groggy in the field.

lines.speaker: WREN
lines.text: You can't stay awake without stopping either. Choose. Tomorrow night.

lines.speaker: ASHCROFT
lines.text: Did you read the books?

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Part of them. The French captain's.

lines.speaker: ASHCROFT
lines.text: Ah. Delacour. 1871. Did you know he returned to Paris afterwards? Wrote three more books, all suppressed by military censorship. Died in 1889, aged 43. Official cause: 'exhaustion'. Real cause: he stopped sleeping.

lines.speaker: ASHCROFT
lines.text: The pattern repeats. Delacour, the Corps of 1876, the Russian Corps of 1915, us now. Always the same kind of people. Always the same kind of encounter.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: And what do those who come back alive have in common?

lines.speaker: ASHCROFT
lines.text: According to my notes? Three things. One: they believed the official account. Two: they never spoke of what they saw. Three: they died young of other causes.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: That is not surviving.

lines.speaker: ASHCROFT
lines.text: Depends on what you call surviving, Vale. I am among them. You will be too. The question is which of the three things you will do differently.

lines.speaker: WARDELL
lines.text: I saw you throw that flask in today's combat. German gas.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: It worked.

lines.speaker: WARDELL
lines.text: It worked. Killed two of them fast. Before dying, they screamed a sound I'll hear in my ear for the rest of my life.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Corporal. If you have something to say, say it.

lines.speaker: WARDELL
lines.text: I don't have orders to say anything. I'm not your superior. But Ashcroft told me something once: using the enemy's weapon brings you closer to him inside. Not physically. Spiritually.

lines.speaker: WARDELL
lines.text: I don't know if I believe in spirit. But I know you're not the same Lieutenant who boarded that ship.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: None of us is.

lines.speaker: WARDELL
lines.text: True. Only some saw something else. Others saw nothing. And those who saw something else rarely come back. Good night, Lieutenant.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He crushes the cigarette against his boot heel and vanishes into the dark.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He is sitting alone in the corner of the camp. Smoking a cigarette you never saw him light.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: …Henry?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He looks up. Smiles. It is the same smile as always.

lines.speaker: HENRY
lines.text: You came.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: You… Loos. You died at Loos, in 1915. I saw—

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He nods. He does not correct. He does not confirm.

lines.speaker: HENRY
lines.text: Sit here.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You sit. He offers you the cigarette. You refuse. He puts it back in his pocket.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You stay silent for a long time. Someone in another camp is playing a harmonica — a song your mother used to sing.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He is there again. In the same corner. As if he had never left.

lines.speaker: HENRY
lines.text: Have you been sleeping?

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Little.

lines.speaker: HENRY
lines.text: Dreams?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He does not insist. You want to ask ten things. You ask none.

lines.speaker: HENRY
lines.text: I don't dream anymore either.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He crushes the cigarette against his boot heel. You recognise the gesture — it was Wardell's. Or it was his, before.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Tomorrow is the General. You know. Everyone knows.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Henry is sitting, hands in his lap. He does not smoke this time.

lines.speaker: HENRY
lines.text: Edmund.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Yes?

lines.speaker: HENRY
lines.text: When you see his face…

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He stops. Looks at his own hands for a long time.

lines.speaker: HENRY
lines.text: …do not look away.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He stands. He touches your shoulder. His hand is cold, as you remember.

lines.speaker: HENRY
lines.text: It will be all right.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He walks out of the camp. You do not see where he goes.

lines.speaker: PETROV
lines.text: Vale. Sit. Tea's almost ready.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: You saved tea for Act Three.

lines.speaker: PETROV
lines.text: Always. Last of the tin Wren brought in January.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He pours slowly. His hands are steady. They always have been.

lines.speaker: PETROV
lines.text: When this is over — one way or the other — I go back to Russia. If there's still a Russia.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: And if there isn't?

lines.speaker: PETROV
lines.text: Then I plant potatoes somewhere. Potatoes don't ask about your past.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He looks at you. Smiles without joy.

lines.speaker: PETROV
lines.text: You'll do what you have to do tomorrow, lieutenant. And I'll be beside you. Not because I was ordered. Because I chose.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Petrov is polishing something you don't recognize — a bronze medallion, Orthodox, worn.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Never seen that before.

lines.speaker: PETROV
lines.text: I don't let anyone see it. It was Fyodor's.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Your brother.

lines.speaker: PETROV
lines.text: My brother. He carried it until 1915. Then I carried it. I don't even know what I'm asking for anymore when I squeeze it. I just ask.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He puts the medallion in the inner pocket. Turns back to the fire.

lines.speaker: PETROV
lines.text: Tomorrow, when the General comes, you'll be out front alone. I know that. But I'll be behind you. And if you fall, I carry you. Like I carried Fyodor.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Petrov—

lines.speaker: PETROV
lines.text: Drink the tea, lieutenant. While it's hot.

lines.speaker: WREN
lines.text: Lieutenant. Let me see that hand.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: It's nothing.

lines.speaker: WREN
lines.text: You're holding it the way Petrov held his shoulder at Ypres. It's something.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: She cleans the cut with a cloth. Her face doesn't change.

lines.speaker: WREN
lines.text: Do you know the difference between a good doctor and a bad one, Vale?

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Diagnosis.

lines.speaker: WREN
lines.text: Courage to lie. The good one lies better. Says “you'll be fine” with conviction even when they know you won't.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: And you?

lines.speaker: WREN
lines.text: I tell the truth. Which is why people end up hating me. Tomorrow I'll tell you the truth, if you need to hear it. Just tell me which truth you want.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Wren has a bottle. Not her first of the day. She offers you some.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Don't drink before an operation.

lines.speaker: WREN
lines.text: Lucky, then. Tomorrow isn't an operation. Tomorrow is something else.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: What is it, then?

lines.speaker: WREN
lines.text: Burial. I don't know. Depends who's burying whom.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: She drinks. Wipes her mouth on her sleeve.

lines.speaker: WREN
lines.text: My father was a trench doctor in the Boer. Came home and never slept in a closed room again. Slept in the garden. In the rain. Preferred it.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: And you?

lines.speaker: WREN
lines.text: I haven't come home yet. Ask me again when I do. If I do.

lines.speaker: ASHCROFT
lines.text: Vale. Sit. I need you to read this.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He hands you a sheet. Ancient Greek. You can't read it.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: I don't know Greek.

lines.speaker: ASHCROFT
lines.text: Doesn't matter. Just hold it while I read.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He reads. Slowly. You don't understand the words but something inside you tightens, like a cable being drawn taut.

lines.speaker: ASHCROFT
lines.text: There. If tomorrow anything tries to enter you wearing a name that isn't yours, this prayer will slow it. It'll give you two, three seconds.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Two, three seconds for what?

lines.speaker: ASHCROFT
lines.text: To decide whether you want to resist. You will have to decide. And it will depend on you.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Ashcroft is sitting with a book on his lap, open, but he isn't reading. He's looking at the fire.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Captain.

lines.speaker: ASHCROFT
lines.text: Vale. Have you ever thought about why Whitehall picked you? Not the other officers. You.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Not much.

lines.speaker: ASHCROFT
lines.text: You should. I did. I read the files. There were eighteen candidates for this posting. You were the only one who lost a brother the way you lost one.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: That's a qualification?

lines.speaker: ASHCROFT
lines.text: It's a requirement. These things find you through the hole loss leaves. If you didn't have the hole, you'd be no use to them. Or to Whitehall. I'm sorry, lieutenant. I should have told you sooner.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Why now?

lines.speaker: ASHCROFT
lines.text: Because tomorrow might be too late.

lines.speaker: WARDELL
lines.text: Lieutenant. I'm playing poker alone. Want in?

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: I don't know poker.

lines.speaker: WARDELL
lines.text: Even better. Sit.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He deals cards. You look at yours. He looks at his. Nobody bets.

lines.speaker: WARDELL
lines.text: My father taught me to play. He used to say: in poker, whoever knows when to quit wins. Not whoever has the best hand.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Your father was a gambler?

lines.speaker: WARDELL
lines.text: My father was a miner. But he knew how to leave a mine that was about to collapse before the others. Saved thirty-seven men in Aberfan in 1902.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He shows the cards. Wins. Gathers them up.

lines.speaker: WARDELL
lines.text: Tomorrow, if I say “let's go,” lieutenant, you're going to listen to me. My father taught me. I'm teaching you.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Wardell is sharpening the bayonet. No drama. Like doing dishes.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Need anything?

lines.speaker: WARDELL
lines.text: I'm fine. You came to me.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: I did.

lines.speaker: WARDELL
lines.text: Tomorrow's going to be ugly. You know that. I know that. But I want to tell you something no one else has.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: WARDELL
lines.text: You're a bad officer, Vale.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You look at him. He keeps sharpening.

lines.speaker: WARDELL
lines.text: Don't look at me like that. You're a bad officer because you listen too much to the enlisted. A good officer orders and that's it. You ask. You weigh. You doubt.

lines.speaker: WARDELL
lines.text: Which is exactly why we follow you. If you were a good officer I'd have deserted already. Good night, lieutenant.
